subject.title: fix(browser): close tracked tabs after gateway restart

question: When a persisted tab cannot re-establish its browser identity for an extended period, should cleanup retain it indefinitely for a possible later lifecycle close or retire it under a bounded, documented stale-record policy?
rationale: The mechanical CDP error normalization is clear, but retention controls trade eventual cleanup against the capacity and availability risk of a bounded durable store in shared browser profiles.

options.title: Add bounded stale-record retirement
options.body: Retire records after a conservative age or repeated identity-unavailable threshold while retaining the explicit no-adoption and profile/browser-fingerprint checks.

options.title: Retain indefinitely
options.body: Keep durable rows until lifecycle cleanup succeeds, accepting that store capacity and new browser opens need another recovery mechanism.

recommendation.title: Add bounded stale-record retirement
recommendation.body: Retire records after a conservative age or repeated identity-unavailable threshold while retaining the explicit no-adoption and profile/browser-fingerprint checks.
